context.rule: 正在 (also 正 or 在) before the verb, and/or 呢 at the end, shows an action in progress; the negative is 没(在)
context.en: He is waiting for a friend.

why: 正在 before the verb, with 呢 at the end, shows an action in progress: 他正在等朋友呢.

not.已经: 已经 means already, a finished action, not one in progress.
not.一边: 一边 comes in pairs (一边……一边……) for two actions at once.
not.有的: 有的 means 'some' and needs a noun to point at; it is not a time word.

context.rule: 正在 (also 正 or 在) before the verb, and/or 呢 at the end, shows an action in progress; the negative is 没(在)
context.en: It's raining outside.

why: 正在 plus 呢 marks something happening right now: 外边正在下雨呢.

not.一边: 一边 links two simultaneous actions; there is only one action here.
not.有的: 有的 means 'some (of them)'; rain is not a group.
not.刚才: 刚才 means 'just now' and describes the past, but 呢 shows it is happening now.

context.rule: 正在 (also 正 or 在) before the verb, and/or 呢 at the end, shows an action in progress; the negative is 没(在)
context.en: He isn't reading; he's sleeping.

why: The negative of 在 + verb is 没(在) + verb: 他没在看书, he isn't reading.

not.呢: 呢 goes at the end of the sentence, not before 看书.
not.吗: 吗 makes a question and cannot sit between 没 and the verb.
not.有的: 有的 means 'some' and has no place after 没.

q: 我给他打电话的时候，他正在___。

context.rule: 正在 (also 正 or 在) before the verb, and/or 呢 at the end, shows an action in progress; the negative is 没(在)
context.en: When I phoned him, he was reading.

why: 正在 ... 呢 wraps the verb: 正在看书呢. With 正在 already there, 呢 closes the phrase.

not.看书了: 了 shows the action is finished; 正在 shows it is going on.
not.有的看书: 有的看书 means 'some read'; it is not a continuing action.
not.可能看书: 可能 means maybe and clashes with 正在, which states what was really happening.

q: 我的朋友，___喜欢茶，有的喜欢咖啡。

context.rule: 有的 means "some of them": it picks out parts of a group and is usually repeated
context.en: Some of my friends like tea, some like coffee.

why: 有的……，有的…… splits a group into parts: some like tea, some like coffee.

not.大家: 大家 means 'everyone'; it cannot be followed by 有的 for 'some'.
not.一边: 一边 pairs actions done together, not groups of people.
not.正在: 正在 shows an action in progress and does not split a group.

q: 教室里的学生，___在写字，有的在看书。

context.rule: 有的 means "some of them": it picks out parts of a group and is usually repeated
context.en: Some of the students in the room are writing, some are reading.

why: 有的 starts the first part of a group and 有的 starts the second: 有的在写字，有的在看书.

not.一边: 一边 joins two actions by one person at the same time.
not.正在: 正在 already appears as 在 later; it does not mean 'some'.
not.明年: 明年 is next year, a time word, and cannot mean 'some'.

context.rule: 有的 means "some of them": it picks out parts of a group and is usually repeated
context.en: Some of these clothes are big, some are small.

why: The second half repeats 有的: 有的大，有的小, some big, some small.

not.一边: 一边 is used before verbs, not before adjectives like 小.
not.正在: 正在 goes before verbs, not before an adjective.
not.先生: 先生 means Mr. or sir, not 'some'.

q: 同学们有的坐车来，有的___来。

context.rule: 有的 means "some of them": it picks out parts of a group and is usually repeated
context.en: Some classmates come by bus, some come by bike.

why: 有的坐车来，有的骑车来: both halves have the same shape, a verb plus 来, so 骑车 fits.

not.在骑车: 在 shows an action in progress; the sentence is a habit, not what is happening now.
not.正骑: 正骑 is not a normal word; the pattern is 正在骑车.
not.一边骑车: 一边 needs a second 一边; here we split classmates into two groups.

context.rule: two actions go on at the same time; put 一边 before each verb
context.en: She listens to music while cooking.

why: 一边……，一边…… pairs two actions at the same time: she listens to music while she cooks.

not.有的: 有的 means 'some' and divides people or things.
not.正在: 正在 does not pair with a following 一边.
not.已经: 已经 means already and does not link two actions.

context.rule: two actions go on at the same time; put 一边 before each verb
context.en: We chat while we walk.

why: 一边走路，一边聊天儿: the second 一边 is already given, so the verb 聊天儿 follows it.

not.一边聊天儿: The 一边 is already written before the blank; adding another repeats it.
not.有的聊天儿: 有的 starts a 'some ...' group, not a second action.
not.明年聊天儿: 明年 is next year and does not fit a sentence about what we do while walking.

context.rule: two actions go on at the same time; put 一边 before each verb
context.en: He watches TV while eating.

why: 他一边吃饭，一边看电视: both 一边 are needed, one for each action.

not.刚才: 刚才 means 'just now'; it does not pair with the first 一边.
not.明年: 明年 means next year, which does not fit the first action.

context.rule: two actions go on at the same time; put 一边 before each verb
context.en: Xiaoyu walks while talking on the phone.

why: After the second 一边 comes a plain verb: 一边打电话，一边走路.

not.一边走路: The sentence already has 一边 before the blank; repeating it is wrong.
not.有的走路: 有的 means 'some' and starts a different pattern.
not.正在走路了: 正在 and 了 do not belong after 一边; one pattern at a time.

context.rule: 了 right after a verb shows the action is done; with an object, the object usually carries a number or other modifier
context.en: I drank a cup of coffee.

why: 了 right after the verb marks a finished action: 我喝了一杯咖啡, I drank a cup of coffee.

not.呢: 呢 goes at the end of a sentence for 'in progress' or 'and you?'; it does not follow the verb here.
not.吗: 吗 makes a question at the end of the sentence.
not.的: 的 links a word to a noun; it does not mark a completed action.

context.rule: 了 right after a verb shows the action is done; with an object, the object usually carries a number or other modifier
context.en: Yesterday she washed three pieces of clothing.

why: 洗了三件衣服: 了 after the verb shows the washing is done, and 昨天 confirms it is past.

not.呢: 呢 shows an action in progress, but 昨天 is the past.
not.吗: 吗 turns a statement into a question; this is a statement.
not.吧: 吧 softens a suggestion; it does not mark a finished action.

context.rule: 了 right after a verb shows the action is done; with an object, the object usually carries a number or other modifier
context.en: Where did you go last night?

why: Asking about a past event ends in 了: 昨天晚上你去哪儿了？

not.吗: 吗 already asks yes/no; with 哪儿 the question word does the asking.
not.的: 的 can stress details of a past event but 你去哪儿的 is not a normal question here.
not.在: 在 means be at or in progress; it does not fit 昨天晚上.

q: 昨天我们在饭馆吃___三个菜。

context.rule: 了 right after a verb shows the action is done; with an object, the object usually carries a number or other modifier
context.en: Yesterday we ate three dishes at the restaurant.

why: 吃了三个菜: 了 after the verb with a quantity shows the eating is complete.

not.呢: 呢 shows an ongoing action, not one finished yesterday.
not.吗: 吗 makes questions at the end.
not.的: 的 does not mark completion after 吃.

context.rule: to deny a completed action put 没(有) before the verb and drop 了; 还没……呢 means "not yet"; ask with ……了吗 or ……了没有
context.en: I didn't have coffee; he did.

why: 没 negates a past action: 我没喝咖啡 means I didn't have coffee. 了 never goes with 没.

not.了: 了 is for a finished action; the negative uses 没 instead.
not.呢: 呢 goes at the end and does not negate.

context.rule: to deny a completed action put 没(有) before the verb and drop 了; 还没……呢 means "not yet"; ask with ……了吗 or ……了没有
context.en: Have you eaten or not?

why: The yes/no form 吃饭了没有？ asks 'have you eaten or not?'

not.不是: 不是 means 'is not' and does not ask about a completed action.
not.不有: We say 没有, not 不有.
not.别的: 别的 means 'other', which makes no sense here.

context.rule: to deny a completed action put 没(有) before the verb and drop 了; 还没……呢 means "not yet"; ask with ……了吗 or ……了没有
context.en: He hasn't gone to the mall yet; he's still at home.

why: 还没……呢 means 'not yet': 他还没去商场呢, and 还在家里 agrees.

not.一边: 一边 pairs two actions done at once.
not.已经: 已经 means already, but the second half says he is still at home.

q: A：你告诉他了吗？ B：还没___呢，等一下。

context.rule: to deny a completed action put 没(有) before the verb and drop 了; 还没……呢 means "not yet"; ask with ……了吗 or ……了没有
context.en: A: Have you told him? B: Not yet, wait a moment.

why: 还没……呢 wraps the plain verb phrase: 还没告诉他呢, not yet.

not.告诉他了: 了 is not used after 没; 没 already marks 'not done'.
not.在告诉他: 在 shows an action in progress, which clashes with 还没.
not.不告诉他: 不告诉他 means 'will not tell him'; B says 'not yet'.

context.rule: one action follows right after another: do A, then B immediately
context.en: I'll go to eat as soon as I finish work.

why: ……了……就…… means 'as soon as ... then ...': 我下了班就去吃饭.

not.和: 和 joins nouns, not two actions in order.
not.或者: 或者 means or, giving a choice.
not.一边: 一边 means doing two things at the same time, not one after the other.

context.rule: one action follows right after another: do A, then B immediately
context.en: He went to class right after eating.

why: 吃了饭就去上课: 了 after the first verb marks it done, then 就 gives the next step at once.

not.呢: 呢 does not follow the verb in this pattern.
not.吗: 吗 makes a question; this is a statement.
not.的: 的 does not mark a completed action.

q: 明天我到了北京___给你打电话。

context.rule: one action follows right after another: do A, then B immediately
context.en: Tomorrow I'll call you as soon as I reach Beijing.

why: 到了北京就给你打电话: 就 links the second action right after the first.

not.和: 和 joins nouns, not two actions in sequence.
not.正在: 正在 means in progress, but the action is in the future and follows 到了.

context.rule: one action follows right after another: do A, then B immediately
context.en: She went to bed right after her shower.

why: 洗了澡就睡觉了: 就 means 'then straight away' after the first action finishes.

not.一边: 一边 means at the same time; she can't shower and sleep together.
not.正在: 正在 shows an action going on, not one after another.

context.rule: 了 at the end of a sentence shows a change of state or a new situation
context.en: It's warmer now, and the flowers are all out.

why: Sentence-final 了 shows a change of state: the weather has become warm.

not.吗: 吗 makes a question, but this is a statement.
not.在: 在 marks an action in progress; 暖和 is a state.
not.把: 把 moves an object before a verb; it is not a sentence ending.

context.rule: 了 at the end of a sentence shows a change of state or a new situation
context.en: He used to be plump, but now he's thin.

why: 以前 ... 现在 ... 了 contrasts then and now: he has become thin, so 瘦了.

not.吗: 吗 would make it a question.
not.在: 在 does not go after an adjective.
not.有: 有 does not mark change; 瘦有 is not Chinese.

context.rule: 了 at the end of a sentence shows a change of state or a new situation
context.en: Look, it's raining outside!

why: 了 at the end shows a new situation: it has started to rain (你看 points to it).

not.吗: 吗 asks a question; 你看 introduces a statement.
not.没: 没 negates a verb and cannot end a sentence.
not.不: 不 cannot end a sentence like this.

q: 我弟弟今年六岁___，明年上小学。

context.rule: 了 at the end of a sentence shows a change of state or a new situation
context.en: My brother is six this year and starts primary school next year.

why: Age with 了 shows a new state: 六岁了 means 'has turned six'.

not.的: 的 does not mark a new age.
not.在: 在 does not follow an age.
not.把: 把 is for objects before verbs, not an ending.

context.rule: something is about to happen; 就要 or 快要 add urgency, and only 就要 can follow a time word
context.en: The film is about to start, let's go in.

why: 要……了 means 'about to': 电影要开始了, the film is about to start.

not.在: 在 shows an action in progress, but the film has not begun.
not.有: 有 means have and does not mean 'about to'.
not.把: 把 brings an object before a verb and does not fit here.

context.rule: something is about to happen; 就要 or 快要 add urgency, and only 就要 can follow a time word
context.en: We have exams next week.

why: 就要……了 means 'will soon'; with a time word like 下个星期 use 就要.

not.正在: 正在 is for what is happening now, not next week.
not.一边: 一边 pairs two actions at once.

context.rule: something is about to happen; 就要 or 快要 add urgency, and only 就要 can follow a time word
context.en: The train is about to leave, hurry!

why: 快要……了 means 'about to': 火车快要开了. The blank takes 要 after 快.

not.就: 快就 is not a pattern; it is 快要 or 就要.
not.是: 是 is 'to be'; 快是开了 is not Chinese.
not.的: 的 does not link 快 and a verb here.

context.rule: something is about to happen; 就要 or 快要 add urgency, and only 就要 can follow a time word
context.en: It's about to rain tomorrow, so don't go out.

why: 就要……了 can follow a time word such as 明天: 明天就要下雨了.

not.快要: 快要 cannot take a specific time word like 明天; use 就要.
not.正在: 正在 is about now, not tomorrow.
not.有的: 有的 means 'some' and does not fit.

context.rule: 能 for ability or possibility, 可以 for permission; both are negated by 不能 (不可以 only for a ban)
context.en: Can you carry this for me?

why: 能 + verb asks whether someone is able or willing: 你能帮我拿一下吗？

not.在: 在 marks an action in progress; it does not ask for help.
not.把: 把 needs an object and verb after it, not 帮.
not.吧: 吧 is a sentence-final particle, not before the verb.

q: 外边下大雨，今天我们不___去爬山了。

context.rule: 能 for ability or possibility, 可以 for permission; both are negated by 不能 (不可以 only for a ban)
context.en: It's pouring outside, so we can't go hiking today.

why: 不能 means conditions don't allow it: heavy rain, so we can't go hiking.

not.在: 不在去 is not a pattern.
not.把: 把 does not go after 不 and before a verb like this.

q: 教室里___吃东西，请出去吃。

context.rule: 能 for ability or possibility, 可以 for permission; both are negated by 不能 (不可以 only for a ban)
context.en: You can't eat in the classroom; please eat outside.

why: 不能 expresses a rule: you cannot eat in the classroom.

not.不是: 不是 means 'is not' and cannot take a verb phrase like this.
not.不有: We say 没有, not 不有.
not.不在: 不在 means 'not at', and 请出去吃 gives a prohibition.

context.rule: 能 for ability or possibility, 可以 for permission; both are negated by 不能 (不可以 only for a ban)
context.en: May I take a look at this book?

why: 可以 asks for permission: 我可以看看吗？ May I take a look?

not.已经: 已经 means already; asking permission uses 可以.
not.一边: 一边 pairs two actions at once.
not.正在: 正在 shows an action going on, not a request.

context.rule: 会 shows a learned skill ("know how to") or a likelihood ("will probably")
context.en: Can you swim or not?

why: 会 means 'can' for a learned skill; the yes/no form 会不会 asks: can you swim or not?

not.能: 能不会 is not a pattern; 能 would need 能不能.
not.得: 得 (děi) means must, and 得不会 is not said.
not.要: 要不会 is not a pattern; the A-not-A form is 会不会.

context.rule: 会 shows a learned skill ("know how to") or a likelihood ("will probably")
context.en: It's cloudy; will it rain this afternoon?

why: 会 also predicts the future: 下午会下雨吗？ Will it rain this afternoon?

not.得: 得 means must; rain is not an obligation.
not.把: 把 moves an object before a verb; it does not predict.
not.有: 有下雨 is not said; use 会 or 要 to predict.

q: 她从小学游泳，所以___游泳。

context.rule: 会 shows a learned skill ("know how to") or a likelihood ("will probably")
context.en: She learned to swim as a child, so she can swim.

why: 会 means can, a skill learned: she learned as a child, so 她会游泳.

not.把: 把 needs an object and does not mean can.
not.的: 的 does not show ability here.
not.吧: 吧 goes at the end of a sentence, not before the verb.

context.rule: 会 shows a learned skill ("know how to") or a likelihood ("will probably")
context.en: I reckon he won't come tomorrow.

why: 不会 + verb predicts 'will not': 他明天不会来, he won't come.

not.的: 不的来 is not Chinese.
not.把: 把 does not follow 不 like this.
not.吧: 吧 ends a sentence and does not go before a verb.

q: 明天有考试，我今晚___看书。

context.rule: 得 means "must" because the situation requires it; the negative is 不用 (no need), not 不得
context.en: There's an exam tomorrow; I have to study tonight.

why: 得 (děi) before a verb means must: tomorrow's exam, so I have to study tonight.

not.把: 把 does not mean must.
not.的: 的 is not used before a verb in this way.
not.吧: 吧 goes at the end of a sentence.

q: A：我得去机场接他吗？ B：___，他自己坐车来。

context.rule: 得 means "must" because the situation requires it; the negative is 不用 (no need), not 不得
context.en: A: Do I have to meet him at the airport? B: No need, he's coming by himself.

why: 不用 means 'no need to'. B answers A's 得 question with 不用: there is no need.

not.不会: 不会 means will not or cannot; the question is about need.
not.不是: 不是 denies a fact, not an obligation.

q: 你不___给我打电话，我已经知道了。

context.rule: 得 means "must" because the situation requires it; the negative is 不用 (no need), not 不得
context.en: You needn't call me; I already know.

why: 不用 + verb means 'needn't': 你不用给我打电话.

not.把: 不把 does not mean needn't.
not.的: 不的 is not a word.
not.吗: 吗 ends a question and cannot sit inside the sentence.

context.rule: 得 means "must" because the situation requires it; the negative is 不用 (no need), not 不得
context.en: It's raining outside; you must take an umbrella.

why: 得 (děi) means must: it rains, so you must take an umbrella.

not.把: 把 does not mean must, and 带 has no object before it here.
not.的: 的 does not go before 带.
not.吗: 吗 comes at the end and makes a question.

context.rule: verb + 得 + adjective says how well or how an action is done; repeat the verb after an object; the negative puts 不 before the adjective
context.en: He plays football very well.

why: The 得 after the verb links it to a description of how: 踢得很好, plays well.

not.的: 的 and 得 sound alike but 的 links nouns; after a verb to describe how, write 得.
not.地: 地 joins an adverb to a verb, as in 慢慢地走.
not.了: 了 marks completion, not how well something is done.

context.rule: verb + 得 + adjective says how well or how an action is done; repeat the verb after an object; the negative puts 不 before the adjective
context.en: How well do you drive?

why: With the 得 pattern the verb is repeated: 开车开得怎么样, how well do you drive?

not.是: 是开车 would mean something else; the verb must repeat.
not.会: 会得 is not a pattern here.
not.在: 在得 is not a pattern.

context.rule: verb + 得 + adjective says how well or how an action is done; repeat the verb after an object; the negative puts 不 before the adjective
context.en: I don't cook very well.

why: After 得 the negative is 不: 做得不太好, not very well.

not.没: 没 negates past events, not how well one does something.
not.非: 非 does not negate in this pattern.

q: 他开车开得___，我有点儿怕。

context.rule: verb + 得 + adjective says how well or how an action is done; repeat the verb after an object; the negative puts 不 before the adjective
context.en: He drives so fast that I'm a little scared.

why: 太快了 follows 得 as the description: drives too fast, and 了 gives the feeling.

not.太快吗: 吗 would make it a question, but the sentence continues.
not.太快的: 的 does not belong after the adjective here.
not.太快过: 过 means ever done, which does not fit.

context.rule: a length of time goes after the verb; with a pronoun object it goes after the pronoun; a final 了 shows it is still going on
context.en: I waited for him for half an hour.

why: A pronoun object goes between 了 and the duration: 等了他半个小时.

not.他了: With a duration, 了 stays right after the verb: 等了他, not 等他了半个小时.
not.的他: 的 does not follow the verb here.
not.了半: This leaves out 他 and splits 半个小时 from its measure word.

context.rule: a length of time goes after the verb; with a pronoun object it goes after the pronoun; a final 了 shows it is still going on
context.en: He sleeps eight hours every day.

why: A duration comes straight after the verb, with no extra word: 睡八个小时.

not.的八: 的 does not go between the verb and a duration.
not.在八: 在 means at or in progress, not a length of time.
not.把八: 把 needs an object after it and does not fit.

context.rule: a length of time goes after the verb; with a pronoun object it goes after the pronoun; a final 了 shows it is still going on
context.en: She talked on the phone for half an hour.

why: When the verb has an object, repeat it: 打电话打了半个小时. 了 goes after the second verb.

not.的: 的 does not mark how long an action lasted.
not.在: 在 shows an action in progress, not a length of time.
not.把: 把 moves an object before the verb, which is not what happens here.

context.rule: a length of time goes after the verb; with a pronoun object it goes after the pronoun; a final 了 shows it is still going on
context.en: He has been learning Chinese for two years now.

why: Duration + 了 at the end shows it has lasted until now: 学了两年了, two years so far.

not.的: 的 does not close a sentence about duration.
not.在: 在 does not end the sentence.
not.过: 过 means had the experience, not 'has lasted until now'.

q: 电影七点开始，他七点半___到。

context.rule: 就 means early, quick or easy (often with 了 at the end); 才 means late, slow or hard ("not until", without 了)
context.en: The film started at seven; he didn't get there until half past.

why: 才 means later or slower than expected: seven-thirty is late for a seven o'clock film.

not.很: 很 means very and does not fit before a time and 到.
not.把: 把 does not fit before 到.
not.的: 的 does not modify 到 like this.

q: 他早上五点___起床了，真早！

context.rule: 就 means early, quick or easy (often with 了 at the end); 才 means late, slow or hard ("not until", without 了)
context.en: He got up at five in the morning, so early!

why: 就 means earlier or sooner than expected: up at five, so early!

not.才: 才 means later than expected, but the speaker says 真早.
not.很: 很 does not link a time to a verb.

q: 路上堵车，汽车开了一个小时___到。

context.rule: 就 means early, quick or easy (often with 了 at the end); 才 means late, slow or hard ("not until", without 了)
context.en: The road was jammed, so the bus took an hour to arrive.

why: 才 stresses it took longer than expected: an hour of travel because of the jam.

not.很: 很 does not fit before 到.
not.把: 把 needs an object and does not fit before 到.

q: 我家离学校很近，走五分钟___到了。

context.rule: 就 means early, quick or easy (often with 了 at the end); 才 means late, slow or hard ("not until", without 了)
context.en: My home is close to school; it's only a five-minute walk.

why: 就 means sooner or easier than expected: only five minutes and you are there.

not.才: 才 would mean the walk took long.
not.很: 很 does not fit before 到了.
not.把: 把 does not fit before 到.

q: ___工作很忙，但是我每天都去运动。

context.rule: although …, but …; 但是 starts the second clause
context.en: Although work is busy, I still exercise every day.

why: 虽然……但是…… means 'although ... but ...': although work is busy, I still exercise.

not.因为: 因为 gives a reason, but the second half is a contrast.
not.所以: 所以 gives a result, not a concession.
not.一边: 一边 pairs two actions at once.

q: 这件衣服虽然很漂亮，___太贵了。

context.rule: although …, but …; 但是 starts the second clause
context.en: This piece of clothing is pretty, but it's too expensive.

why: 虽然 sets up the first half, so 但是 starts the contrast: pretty, but too expensive.

not.因为: 因为 gives a reason; this is a contrast.
not.所以: 所以 gives a result and does not mark a contrast.
not.才: 才 means 'only then' and does not mark a contrast.

q: 我虽然很累，___还想去看比赛。

context.rule: although …, but …; 但是 starts the second clause
context.en: I'm tired, but I still want to see the match.

why: 虽然很累，但是还想去: 但是 introduces the unexpected opposite.

not.所以: 所以 means so; being tired does not lead to wanting to go.
not.因为: 因为 gives a reason, but the second half contrasts.
not.虽然: 虽然 is already used earlier; the second half needs 但是.

q: 这家商场___很大，但是东西不太多。

context.rule: although …, but …; 但是 starts the second clause
context.en: This mall is big, but it doesn't have much stock.

why: 虽然 begins the first half: although the mall is big, 但是 the stock is limited.

not.所以: 所以 begins a result, not a concession.
not.因为: 因为 gives a reason, not a concession.
not.比较: 比较 means fairly or rather, and cannot pair with 但是.

context.rule: because …, so …; one of the two can be left out
context.en: It rained yesterday, so I didn't go hiking.

why: 因为……所以…… means 'because ... so ...': because it rained, I didn't go hiking.

not.虽然: 虽然 would need 但是.
not.但是: 但是 starts a clause and cannot open the first half.

q: 因为今天太冷了，___我们不出去了。

context.rule: because …, so …; one of the two can be left out
context.en: It's too cold today, so we're not going out.

why: 因为 gives the reason and 所以 the result: too cold, so we're staying in.

not.因为: 因为 is already used in the first half.
not.虽然: 虽然 needs 但是 and cannot follow 因为.
not.但是: 但是 shows contrast, but the cold leads to staying in.

q: 因为她明天有考试，___今晚不能出去玩儿。

context.rule: because …, so …; one of the two can be left out
context.en: She has an exam tomorrow, so she can't go out tonight.

why: 因为……所以……: the exam is the reason, so she can't go out.

not.但是: 但是 shows contrast, but the exam is a cause.
not.才: 才 means 'only then' and does not link cause and result.

context.rule: because …, so …; one of the two can be left out
context.en: I was busy, so I didn't go.

why: 因为 gives the reason, and 所以 follows: I was busy, so I didn't go.

not.虽然: 虽然 would need 但是, not 所以.
not.但是: 但是 cannot start the sentence before 忙.
not.一边: 一边 pairs two actions at once.

context.rule: Verb + 过 says you have done something before. Negative: 没(有) + verb + 过. Question: verb + 过 + object + 没有.
context.en: I have never eaten this kind of dish.

why: 过 after the verb marks experience: 吃过 means have eaten before, and 从来没 stresses never.

not.了: 了 marks a finished action, but 从来没 is about whole life experience.
not.着: 着 shows a continuing state, not experience.
not.的: 的 does not mark experience.

context.rule: Verb + 过 says you have done something before. Negative: 没(有) + verb + 过. Question: verb + 过 + object + 没有.
context.en: Have you ever studied Chinese?

why: 学过 asks about experience: have you ever studied Chinese? 没有 gives the yes/no form.

not.吗: 吗 and 没有 both make the question; one is enough, and 吗 does not go before 中文.
not.的: 的 does not mark experience.

context.rule: Verb + 过 says you have done something before. Negative: 没(有) + verb + 过. Question: verb + 过 + object + 没有.
context.en: He has not been to Beijing yet.

why: 没 negates 过: 还没去过 means has not been yet.

not.不: 不去过 is wrong; 过 is negated with 没.

context.rule: Verb + 过 says you have done something before. Negative: 没(有) + verb + 过. Question: verb + 过 + object + 没有.
context.en: Have you ever been to the Summer Palace?

why: The yes/no tail for a 过 question is 没有: 去过……没有？

not.没吗: 没 and 吗 do not go together.
not.不有: We say 没有, not 不有.

context.rule: Stress the time, place or manner of something that already happened: 是 + detail + verb + 的.
context.en: He came yesterday.

why: 是……的 stresses details of a past event, here when: 他是昨天来的. 的 closes the pattern.

not.地: 地 joins an adverb to a verb.

context.rule: Stress the time, place or manner of something that already happened: 是 + detail + verb + 的.
context.en: How did you get there?

why: 是……的 asks about the way an action was done: 你是怎么去的？

not.有: 有 is have; it does not make 怎么去的 a question.
not.在: 在 means in progress and does not fit.
not.很: 很 is very and does not fit.

context.rule: Stress the time, place or manner of something that already happened: 是 + detail + verb + 的.
context.en: I went to Shanghai by plane.

why: 坐飞机 means go by plane; 是……的 stresses the means: 我是坐飞机去的.

not.在: 在飞机 would mean 'in the plane'; use 坐.
not.了: 了 does not go inside the 是……的 frame.
not.过: 过 marks experience, not a way of travelling.

context.rule: Stress the time, place or manner of something that already happened: 是 + detail + verb + 的.
context.en: We met at school.

why: 在 + place says where it happened: 我们是在学校认识的.

not.跟: 跟 means with a person, not at a place.
not.有: 有 does not give a place.

q: 这本书我看了三___，都看懂了。

context.point: 次 / 遍 / 一下儿 after the verb
context.rule: A number + 次 / 遍 counts how often; 一下儿 makes it short and casual. A noun object goes after the count, a pronoun object before it.
context.en: I read this book three times through and understood all of it.

why: 遍 counts the whole of an action from start to finish: 看了三遍, read it through three times.

not.个: 个 is a general measure for nouns, not for repeating a whole action.
not.把: 把 counts things with handles, not times.

context.point: 次 / 遍 / 一下儿 after the verb
context.rule: A number + 次 / 遍 counts how often; 一下儿 makes it short and casual. A noun object goes after the count, a pronoun object before it.
context.en: Please wait for me a moment.

why: 一下儿 after the verb makes it short and light: 等我一下儿, wait a moment.

not.一遍: 一遍 counts doing something through once, not a short wait.
not.一点儿: 一点儿 means a little of something, not a short time.
not.一个: 一个 does not suit 等 here.

context.point: 次 / 遍 / 一下儿 after the verb
context.rule: A number + 次 / 遍 counts how often; 一下儿 makes it short and casual. A noun object goes after the count, a pronoun object before it.
context.en: He has been to Beijing three times.

why: 次 counts how many times: 去过三次, been three times.

context.point: 次 / 遍 / 一下儿 after the verb
context.rule: A number + 次 / 遍 counts how often; 一下儿 makes it short and casual. A noun object goes after the count, a pronoun object before it.
context.en: I called him twice, but he didn't hear.

why: A pronoun object goes before the times: 叫了他两次.

not.的: 的 does not go between 叫了 and a number.
not.着: 着 does not fit after 了.

context.point: 次 / 遍 / 一下儿 after the verb
context.rule: A number + 次 / 遍 counts how often; 一下儿 makes it short and casual. A noun object goes after the count, a pronoun object before it.
context.en: I have seen this film twice through.

why: 遍 counts a whole viewing from start to end: 看过两遍.

not.个: 个 does not count how many times.
not.本: 本 counts books; films aren't counted with it.

context.rule: Besides X there is more (还 / 也), or X is left out and the rest all do it (都).
context.en: I go to work every day except weekends.

why: 除了……以外 means 'except' or 'besides': 除了周末以外, apart from weekends.

not.在: 在 means at, not except.

q: 除了小王以外，同学们___去过上海。

context.rule: Besides X there is more (还 / 也), or X is left out and the rest all do it (都).
context.en: All the classmates except Xiao Wang have been to Shanghai.

why: 都 sums up the rest: 同学们都去过, all of the others have been.

not.再: 再 means again in the future.

q: 除了游泳___，他也喜欢打篮球。

context.rule: Besides X there is more (还 / 也), or X is left out and the rest all do it (都).
context.en: Besides swimming, he also likes basketball.

why: The frame is 除了……以外: besides swimming, he also likes basketball.

q: 除了上海以外，我还去过___。

context.rule: Besides X there is more (还 / 也), or X is left out and the rest all do it (都).
context.en: Besides Shanghai, I have also been to Beijing.

why: After 还, a place with 过: 还去过北京. The blank is just the place.

not.去北京: 去 is already there before the blank.
not.过北京: 过 is already there before the blank.
not.北京过: 过 follows the verb, not the noun.

context.rule: Verb + 着 describes a state that lasts: 门开着. Negative: 没 + verb + 着. Question: …着没有？ It can also show the manner of another action: 喝着咖啡聊天儿.
context.en: A person is standing at the door.

why: 着 after a verb shows a lasting state: 站着 means standing there.

not.吗: 吗 goes at the end of a question.
not.地: 地 joins an adverb to a verb, but 站 is the verb here.
not.得: 得 links a verb to how well it is done.

context.rule: Verb + 着 describes a state that lasts: 门开着. Negative: 没 + verb + 着. Question: …着没有？ It can also show the manner of another action: 喝着咖啡聊天儿.
context.en: The light isn't on; the room is dark.

why: 没开着 means the light is not left on; 着 marks the lasting state.

not.地: 地 joins a describing word to a verb.
not.得: 得 links a verb to a description.
not.吗: 吗 makes a question at the end.

context.rule: Verb + 着 describes a state that lasts: 门开着. Negative: 没 + verb + 着. Question: …着没有？ It can also show the manner of another action: 喝着咖啡聊天儿.
context.en: Is your phone on?

why: 开着 means left on, a continuing state; the question ends in 没有.

not.吗: 吗 and 没有 both make a question, and 吗 does not sit after 开.
not.地: 地 joins an adverb to a verb.
not.得: 得 links a verb to how well it's done.

context.rule: Verb + 着 describes a state that lasts: 门开着. Negative: 没 + verb + 着. Question: …着没有？ It can also show the manner of another action: 喝着咖啡聊天儿.
context.en: They cook while listening to music.

why: Verb + 着 + second verb shows how the second action is done: 听着音乐做饭, cooking while listening.

not.地: 地 follows an adverb, not a verb like 听.
not.得: 得 needs a description after it.
not.吗: 吗 goes at the end of a question.

context.rule: Put 地 between an adverb-like adjective and the verb: 认真地写. For the result after a verb use 得: 写得很认真.
context.en: She listens to the teacher carefully.

why: 认真 describes how she listens, so it needs 地 before the verb: 认真地听.

not.的: 的 links to a noun, not to a verb.
not.得: 得 comes after a verb, not before.
not.着: 着 marks a continuing state, not manner.

context.rule: Put 地 between an adverb-like adjective and the verb: 认真地写. For the result after a verb use 得: 写得很认真.
context.en: He walked slowly into the classroom.

why: 慢慢 describes how he walked, so 地 goes before the verb: 慢慢地走.

not.的: 的 links to a noun.

context.rule: Put 地 between an adverb-like adjective and the verb: 认真地写. For the result after a verb use 得: 写得很认真.
context.en: She said happily, "Hello!"

why: 很高兴 describes how she said it: 高兴地说, said happily.

not.的: 的 links to a noun.
not.得: 得 comes after a verb to describe it.

context.rule: Put 地 between an adverb-like adjective and the verb: 认真地写. For the result after a verb use 得: 写得很认真.
context.en: He writes characters very carefully.

why: The verb comes first and 得 links it to how well it's done: 写得很认真.

not.地: 地 comes before the verb: 认真地写. After the verb, use 得.
not.的: 的 links to a noun.

context.rule: Doubling an adjective makes it stronger: 大 → 大大, 高兴 → 高高兴兴 (AABB). As a manner before a verb, AABB needs 地.
context.en: His room is kept very tidy.

why: Two-syllable adjectives double as AABB: 整齐 becomes 整整齐齐, very tidy.

not.整整齐: AABB needs all four syllables: 整整齐齐.
not.整齐整齐: 整齐整齐 is ABAB, which is how verbs double, not adjectives.
not.整齐齐齐: 整齐齐齐 is not a pattern.

context.rule: Doubling an adjective makes it stronger: 大 → 大大, 高兴 → 高高兴兴 (AABB). As a manner before a verb, AABB needs 地.
context.en: She has big, big eyes.

why: A one-syllable adjective doubles as AA: 大 becomes 大大, 大大的 big and round.

not.大大大: Three times is not a pattern.
not.大的大: 大的大 is not a pattern.
not.很大大: 很 does not go with the doubled form.

q: 孩子们高高兴兴___回家了。

context.rule: Doubling an adjective makes it stronger: 大 → 大大, 高兴 → 高高兴兴 (AABB). As a manner before a verb, AABB needs 地.
context.en: The children went home happily.

why: A doubled adjective before a verb takes 地: 高高兴兴地回家.

not.着: 着 marks a lasting state, not manner.

q: 教室里很多学生安安静静___坐着。

context.rule: Doubling an adjective makes it stronger: 大 → 大大, 高兴 → 高高兴兴 (AABB). As a manner before a verb, AABB needs 地.
context.en: Many students sit quietly in the classroom.

why: 安安静静 describes how they sit, so 地 follows: 安安静静地坐着.

not.着: 着 is already after 坐.

q: 作业还没做___，我不能出去玩儿。

context.rule: A word right after the verb tells the result: 做完, 听清楚, 打错. Negative: 没(有) + verb + complement. Question: …了没有？
context.en: I haven't finished my homework, so I can't go out to play.

why: 完 after the verb is a result complement meaning finished: 做完, done doing.

not.的: 的 does not show a result.

context.rule: A word right after the verb tells the result: 做完, 听清楚, 打错. Negative: 没(有) + verb + complement. Question: …了没有？
context.en: Sorry, I didn't hear what you said clearly.

why: 听清楚 means to hear clearly; 清楚 is the result of 听.

not.好吃: 好吃 means tasty; it describes food.
not.高兴: 高兴 means happy and cannot be the result of hearing.

q: 我打___电话了，这不是他家。

context.rule: A word right after the verb tells the result: 做完, 听清楚, 打错. Negative: 没(有) + verb + complement. Question: …了没有？
context.en: I dialled the wrong number; this isn't his home.

why: 打错 means dialled wrong; 错 is the result: 我打错电话了.

not.容易: 容易 means easy and does not say whether the call was right.

context.rule: A word right after the verb tells the result: 做完, 听清楚, 打错. Negative: 没(有) + verb + complement. Question: …了没有？
context.en: Did you see that person?

why: 看见 means actually see; 见 is the result that proves the looking worked.

not.看: 看看 does not give a result; 看 is already in the sentence.
not.的: 的 does not give a result.
not.不: 不 is a negative and cannot give the result.

context.rule: A word right after the verb tells the result: 做完, 听清楚, 打错. Negative: 没(有) + verb + complement. Question: …了没有？
context.en: I haven't finished eating yet.

why: 完 right after the verb shows it is finished; the negative is 没吃完.

not.完了: 完了 means it's all over; 完 alone sits after the verb.
not.了: 了 would give 没吃了, which is wrong after 没.
not.的: 的 gives no result.

q: 他昨天睡___十一点才起床。

context.rule: After a verb, 到 means reaching a place, a time or a goal.
context.en: He slept until eleven o'clock yesterday.

why: 到 after a verb can mean 'until' a time: 睡到十一点, slept until eleven.

not.在: 在 shows location: 睡在床上.

context.rule: After a verb, 到 means reaching a place, a time or a goal.
context.en: I found my watch!

why: 找到 means found; 到 shows the search succeeded.

not.在: 找在 is not a result.
not.的: 的 does not show a result.

q: 这封信下个星期才能寄___。

context.rule: After a verb, 到 means reaching a place, a time or a goal.
context.en: This letter won't arrive until next week.

why: 寄到 means sent so that it arrives: 到 marks the destination reached.

not.在: 寄在 puts the letter at a place, not a destination.
not.的: 的 does not show a result.

context.rule: After a verb, 到 means reaching a place, a time or a goal.
context.en: We waited until eight in the evening.

why: 等到晚上八点 means waited until eight, with 到 for the end time.

not.在: 等在 means wait at a place.
not.给: 等给 is not a pattern.
not.对: 等对 is not a pattern.

context.rule: Two events follow each other at once: 一 + first event, 就 + second event.
context.en: As soon as I get home I'll call you.

why: 一……就…… means 'as soon as ... then ...': 我一到家就给你打电话.

not.才: 才 means only then, later than expected.

context.rule: Two events follow each other at once: 一 + first event, 就 + second event.
context.en: As soon as he gets up he starts looking at his phone.

why: 他一起床就开始看手机: 一 and 就 link two actions in quick succession.

context.rule: Two events follow each other at once: 一 + first event, 就 + second event.
context.en: My little sister laughed as soon as she saw the kitten.

why: The first half is 一 + verb: 一看见小猫就笑了, laughed as soon as she saw it.

not.要: 要 means want or about to.

context.rule: Two events follow each other at once: 一 + first event, 就 + second event.
context.en: As soon as it gets dark, there are fewer people on the road.

why: 天一黑，……就少了: 一 first, then 就 for the result right after.

not.才: 才 means only then; fewer people comes soon, not late.
not.把: 把 does not fit before 少.

context.rule: verb + 来 if it moves toward the speaker, + 去 if away; a place goes before 来 / 去
context.en: I'm upstairs; come on up.

why: 来 points the movement toward the speaker. The speaker is upstairs, so 上来 means come up to me.

not.去: 上去 would move away from the speaker, but the speaker is upstairs.
not.下: 下 means down, but the speaker is above.
not.进: 进 means enter, not go up.

context.rule: verb + 来 if it moves toward the speaker, + 去 if away; a place goes before 来 / 去
context.en: I'm waiting downstairs, come down quickly!

why: The speaker is downstairs, so coming down is toward the speaker: 下来.

not.去: 下去 moves away from the speaker.
not.上: 上 means up; the speaker is below.

q: 我在家，妈妈从商店买回___一些水果。

context.rule: verb + 来 if it moves toward the speaker, + 去 if away; a place goes before 来 / 去
context.en: I'm at home, and Mum has bought some fruit and brought it back.

why: The speaker is at home, so 买回来 moves the fruit toward the speaker.

not.去: 回去 moves away from the speaker.
not.上: 买回上 is not a pattern.
not.下: 买回下 is not a pattern.

q: 我在学校，这本书我晚上带回家___。

context.rule: verb + 来 if it moves toward the speaker, + 去 if away; a place goes before 来 / 去
context.en: I'm at school; I'll take this book home tonight.

why: The speaker is at school and the book goes home, away from the speaker: 带回家去.

not.来: 来 would mean toward the speaker, but home is away from school.
not.上: 带回家上 is not a pattern.
not.下: 带回家下 is not a pattern.

context.point: 请 / 叫 / 让 (asking someone to do something)
context.rule: A + 请 / 叫 / 让 + B + verb: B does it; 请 is polite and can mean invite
context.en: Mum tells me to come home early.

why: 叫 + person + verb is 'tell someone to do': 妈妈叫我早点儿回家.

not.对: 对 means towards a person, not 'tell someone to'.
not.在: 在 marks location.

context.point: 请 / 叫 / 让 (asking someone to do something)
context.rule: A + 请 / 叫 / 让 + B + verb: B does it; 请 is polite and can mean invite
context.en: I'd like to invite a friend to dinner.

why: 请 + person + verb means invite or ask: 请朋友吃饭, treat a friend to a meal.

not.在: 在 marks location.

context.point: 请 / 叫 / 让 (asking someone to do something)
context.rule: A + 请 / 叫 / 让 + B + verb: B does it; 请 is polite and can mean invite
context.en: Please help me carry this bag.

why: 帮我拿 means help me carry: 帮 + person + verb.

not.在: 在 marks location.

context.point: 请 / 叫 / 让 (asking someone to do something)
context.rule: A + 请 / 叫 / 让 + B + verb: B does it; 请 is polite and can mean invite
context.en: If he doesn't let me go, I won't go.

why: 让 + person + verb means let or allow: 他不让我走, he won't let me go.

not.在: 在 marks location.

context.rule: 要是 states the condition; 就 comes in the second part
context.en: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.

why: 要是……就…… means 'if ... then ...': 要是明天下雨，我们就不去了.

not.因为: 因为 gives a reason, not a condition.
not.虽然: 虽然 gives a concession, which needs 但是.
not.所以: 所以 means so and would need a cause first.

q: 要是你饿了，___先吃点儿东西吧。

context.rule: 要是 states the condition; 就 comes in the second part
context.en: If you're hungry, have something to eat first.

why: In 要是……就……, 就 starts the result: if you're hungry, then eat first.

q: 你要是有空儿，___给我打电话。

context.rule: 要是 states the condition; 就 comes in the second part
context.en: If you're free, call me.

why: 要是 gives the condition and 就 the result: if you're free, then call me.

context.rule: 要是 states the condition; 就 comes in the second part
context.en: If you don't like it, don't buy it.

why: 要是 opens the condition: if you don't like it, 就 don't buy it.

not.虽然: 虽然 would need 但是.

q: 他是我最好的朋友，我___能忘了他呢？

not.把: 把 would need an object after it, like 把蛋糕吃完.

context.point: Where things go in a passive
context.rule: Negatives and 可能 / 想 go before 被 / 叫 / 让. If the doer is unknown or unimportant, 被 can come straight before the verb, or 人 can stand for "someone".
context.en: He wasn't criticized by the teacher.

why: 没 goes before 被: 他没被老师批评, he wasn't criticized.

not.把: 把 and 被 do not mix.
not.在: 在被 is not a pattern.

q: 我的自行车可能___人骑走了。

context.point: Where things go in a passive
context.rule: Negatives and 可能 / 想 go before 被 / 叫 / 让. If the doer is unknown or unimportant, 被 can come straight before the verb, or 人 can stand for "someone".
context.en: Someone may have ridden off on my bike.

why: 让 + doer + verb is a spoken passive, and 可能 comes before it: 可能让人骑走了.

not.在: 在 marks location.

q: 他忙得___吃饭的时间也没有。

context.rule: "Even …": 连 puts a word in the spotlight, and 也 or 都 follows to say that even this is so, which shows how extreme things are.
context.en: He is so busy he doesn't even have time to eat.

why: 连……也没有 means 'not even': 连吃饭的时间也没有.

not.把: 把 needs a verb.

q: 这个问题太容易了，连孩子___会做。

context.rule: "Even …": 连 puts a word in the spotlight, and 也 or 都 follows to say that even this is so, which shows how extreme things are.
context.en: This question is so easy that even a child can do it.

why: 连……都/也 + verb stresses 'even': 连孩子都会做.

not.就: 就 means then or at once.

context.rule: "Even …": 连 puts a word in the spotlight, and 也 or 都 follows to say that even this is so, which shows how extreme things are.
context.en: I have a cold; I can't even eat.

why: 连饭也吃不下 means can't even eat; 也 follows 连 + the noun.

context.rule: "Even …": 连 puts a word in the spotlight, and 也 or 都 follows to say that even this is so, which shows how extreme things are.
context.en: He is so tired he doesn't even want to talk.

why: 连话也不想说 means doesn't even want to talk; 连 starts the 'even' pattern.

context.rule: The thing acted on can be the subject with no 被: thing + verb + result + 了. Common with 好 / 完.
context.en: Have all the rooms been tidied?

why: The thing (房间) is the topic, so a plain verb + 好 shows it is done: 收拾好了, with no 被 needed.

not.收拾了: 收拾了好了 doubles up the 了.
not.收拾得: 得 needs a description after the verb, and 好了 is not one here.
not.在收拾: 在收拾 means in progress, not finished.

context.rule: The thing acted on can be the subject with no 被: thing + verb + result + 了. Common with 好 / 完.
context.en: Is the meal ready?

why: 做好 means finished making, so 饭做好了吗 means is the meal ready? No 被 needed.

not.的: 的 gives no result.
not.吗: 吗 is already added after 了.
not.地: 地 joins an adverb to a verb.

context.rule: The thing acted on can be the subject with no 被: thing + verb + result + 了. Common with 好 / 完.
context.en: The letter has already been sent.

why: 寄走 means sent off; the letter is the topic, and no 被 is needed.

not.寄得: 寄得 needs a description after it.
not.寄地: 地 joins an adverb to a verb.

context.rule: The thing acted on can be the subject with no 被: thing + verb + result + 了. Common with 好 / 完.
context.en: The homework isn't finished yet.

why: 写完 means finished writing; 还没写完 says the homework is not done, with no 被 needed.

not.被: 被 needs a doer after it.
not.把: 把 needs an object after it.
not.在: 在写完 is wrong; 在 marks something in progress.

context.rule: 刚 + verb: something happened just a moment ago. 刚 goes right before the verb.
context.en: I've just arrived in Beijing and am not used to it yet.

why: 刚 before a verb means 'just': 刚到北京, just arrived.

not.吗: 吗 ends a question.
not.很: 很 means very and does not fit before 到.
not.把: 把 needs an object.

q: 我刚上大学___，一个朋友也没有。

context.rule: 刚 + verb: something happened just a moment ago. 刚 goes right before the verb.
context.en: When I had just started university, I didn't have a single friend.

why: 刚上大学的时候 means when I had just started university; 的时候 marks the time.

not.的时间: 的时间 means 'the time of', not 'when'.
not.在时候: 在时候 is not a pattern.

q: 我哥哥___回国，现在在休息。

context.rule: 刚 + verb: something happened just a moment ago. 刚 goes right before the verb.
context.en: My older brother has just returned home and is resting.

why: 刚 + verb means 'just did it': 刚回国, has just returned.

not.吗: 吗 ends a question.

context.rule: 刚 + verb: something happened just a moment ago. 刚 goes right before the verb.
context.en: The teacher has just left, so go and find him quickly.

why: 刚走 means has just left, so there is a chance to catch him.

not.吗: 吗 ends a question.

context.rule: 向 = towards a person or direction; 给 = to / for someone; 为 = for the sake of.
context.en: Please turn right.

why: 向 + direction + verb means 'toward': 请向右拐, turn right.

not.给: 给 is followed by a person.
not.为: 为 gives a reason or beneficiary.
not.把: 把 needs an object.

q: 妈妈___我买了一件新衣服。

context.rule: 向 = towards a person or direction; 给 = to / for someone; 为 = for the sake of.
context.en: Mum bought me a new piece of clothing.

why: 给 + person marks who it is done for: 给我买, bought for me.

not.把: 把 needs an object.

context.rule: 向 = towards a person or direction; 给 = to / for someone; 为 = for the sake of.
context.en: We're all happy for you.

why: 为你高兴 means happy for you; 为 marks the person the feeling is for.

not.向: 向 means toward a person or direction.
not.把: 把 needs an object.

context.rule: 向 = towards a person or direction; 给 = to / for someone; 为 = for the sake of.
context.en: Tomorrow I'll say goodbye to the teacher.

why: 向老师告别 means say goodbye to the teacher; 向 marks the person addressed.

not.往: 往 is for direction of travel.
not.在: 在 marks location.

context.rule: verb + 不了 = can't (do it, finish it, or let it happen).
context.en: So many books; I can't carry them all by myself.

why: 拿不了 means can't carry all, as there are too many: 不了 (liǎo) marks 'unable'.

not.的了: 拿的了 is wrong; 得 or 不 goes there.
not.完不: 完不 is in the wrong order.

context.rule: verb + 不了 = can't (do it, finish it, or let it happen).
context.en: I'm busy tomorrow, so I can't go.

why: 去不了 means can't go because of a reason: 不 sits between the verb and 了 (liǎo).

not.没: 去没了 is not a pattern.
not.吗: 吗 ends a question.

context.rule: verb + 不了 = can't (do it, finish it, or let it happen).
context.en: This is too hard; I can't do it.

why: 做不了 means unable to do; 不了 (liǎo) follows the verb.

not.没了: 做没了 is not a pattern.
not.不去: 不去 means will not go.
not.吗了: 吗了 is not a pattern.

context.rule: verb + 不了 = can't (do it, finish it, or let it happen).
context.en: Nobody can forget how good he was.

why: 忘不了 means cannot forget; 谁都 gives 'nobody'.

not.没了: 忘没了 is not a pattern.
not.别了: 别了 is not a pattern.
not.吗了: 吗了 is not a pattern.
